title: Improving Reasoning with Rollout Agreement for Group-Based Policy Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2610.34951v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent methods for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) use rollout diversity to improve reasoning performance or training efficiency. Despite these gains, the extent to which differences among correct-answer rollouts reflect useful alternative reasoning or unresolved errors remains poorly understood. We investigate this question through a blind paired analysis of a model trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), comparing the highest- and lowest-agreement correct-answer traces for the same problem. Across 126 pairs, low-agreement traces have more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35% vs. 22%), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on these findings, we propose RoAR (Rollout-Agreement Reward), which adds reasoning-level agreement to GRPO's rewards for verified-correct rollouts. translated_title: 利用展开一致性改进基于分组的策略优化中的推理能力
translated_abstract: 近期的可验证奖励强化学习方法利用展开多样性来提升推理性能或训练效率。尽管取得了这些进展，正确答案展开之间的差异究竟反映了有用的替代推理路径，还是尚未解决的错误，仍然缺乏充分的理解。我们通过对一个使用分组相对策略优化训练的模型进行盲测配对分析来研究这一问题，比较同一问题中一致性最高与最低的正确答案推理轨迹。在126对样本中，低一致性轨迹比高一致性轨迹包含更多的虚假推理（35% 对 22%），包括内部自相矛盾和对题目条件的误用。基于这些发现，我们提出了RoAR（展开一致性奖励），它在GRPO对已验证正确展开的奖励基础上加入了推理级别的一致性信号。RoAR从现有的同策略展开组中计算该信号，无需……
tldr: 该研究发现GRPO训练中正确答案展开间的低一致性往往伴随更多虚假推理，并提出RoAR方法，在奖励中加入推理级别的一致性信号，以提升大模型推理的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that low agreement among correct-answer rollouts in GRPO training correlates with more spurious reasoning, and proposes RoAR, which augments rewards with reasoning-level agreement signals to improve model reliability in reasoning.
